en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (5) 17.1.
Kusala-ttika, Vedanā-ttika
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.

Dependent upon a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, there arises an unwholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition. [Dependent upon] a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling...

Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, a state that is neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition …pe… dependent on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling,
states that are neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling and states that are neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arise by way of root condition … five.

Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, there arises an unwholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with pleasant feeling,
there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition … pe …

Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling and neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling by way of root-condition … five.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling … [and so on] by way of root-condition … five.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling … [and so on].

A associated state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, an unwholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arises... [by way of root condition].
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arises... [by way of root condition].
And neither-unwholesome-nor-indeterminate states associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arise by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated. Under root: thirteen;
under object: nine... pe... under result: three... pe... under non-disappearance: thirteen. Non-root, non-object, etc.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, by way of the not-root condition … three.

Dependent on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, by way of the not-object condition. Dependent on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling … [and so forth].

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling by way of not-object condition. Dependent on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling,
there arise states that are neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling and states that are neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling by way of not-object condition… three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor associated with unpleasant feeling by way of not-object condition... three.

Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with unpleasant feeling by way of not-object condition. [Dependent on] an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling...

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling, a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling,
states that are neither wholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling and states that are neither unwholesome nor associated with pleasant feeling arise by way of object condition.
… three. (Abbreviated. With not-root condition there are three;

with not-object condition, nine; with not-predominance condition, thirteen … pe … with not-prenascence condition, thirteen … pe … with not-jhāna and not-path conditions, three; with not-dissociation condition, nine … pe … with not-disappearance condition, nine.
With root condition and not-object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, three [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.
(The Chapter on Co-nascence, the Chapter on Conditions, the Chapter on Support, the Chapter on Conjoined, and the Chapter on Associated are the same as the Chapter on Dependent.
A wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition, by way of root condition, for an unwholesome state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling … pe …

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are thirteen; in object condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), eighteen; in predominance condition (adhipati-paccaya), seventeen; in proximity condition (anantara-paccaya), nine ... pe ... in conascence condition (sahajāta-paccaya), thirteen;

in mutuality condition (aññamañña-paccaya), nine; in dependence condition (nissaya-paccaya), thirteen; in strong-dependence condition (upanissaya-paccaya), eighteen; in postnascence condition (pacchājāta-paccaya), nine;

in kamma condition (kamma-paccaya), thirteen; in resultant condition (vipāka-paccaya), three; in nutriment condition (āhāra-paccaya) ... pe ... in path condition (magga-paccaya), thirteen; in association condition (sampayutta-paccaya), nine; in dissociation condition (vippayutta-paccaya), nine ... pe ...
Thirteen [factors] when not dissociated. (The section on questions should also be expanded in detail. 17.1.1.
Unwholesome Section: Root Condition.

Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with painful feeling, there arises a non-unwholesome state not associated with painful feeling by way of root condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with painful feeling,
there arises a non-wholesome state not associated with painful feeling by way of root condition … pe …

Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with painful feeling, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, and which are neither unwholesome nor associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five;

under object condition, six; under predominance condition, five ... [and so on] ... under conascence condition, eight ... [and so on] ... under repetition condition, three ... [and so on] ... under result condition, three ... [and so on] ... under jhāna and path conditions, five ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance condition, eight.

17.1.2. Negative Form of the Indeterminate Section (Abyākatapada Paccanīya) In dependence on an indeterminate state associated with painful feeling, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with painful feeling.

A state associated with painful feeling arises by way of the condition of not-root. Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with painful feeling, an unwholesome state not associated with painful feeling arises by way of the condition of not-root.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with painful feeling, a state not wholesome and not associated with painful feeling [arises]... by way of the condition of not-root.
States that are associated with the indeterminate and not associated with painful feeling arise without the root condition (*na-hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated.
Three for the absence of root, three for the absence of object, eight for the absence of predominance … [etc. … five for the absence of prenascence … [etc.

… five for the absence of result, three for the absence of jhāna, the absence of path, and the absence of association, three for the absence of absence and the absence of disappearance. (The Section on Co-nascence is also [to be treated] thus.)
... [and so on] ... the section on questions (*pañhāvāra*) should also be expanded in detail.

Dependent on a wholesome state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

(Abbreviated. There are thirteen [conditions] under root, nine under object (*ārammaṇa*) ... [and so on] ... three under result (*vipāka*) ... [and so on] ... thirteen under non-disappearance (*avigata*). (The expansion applies everywhere.)
